```{r}
ppl_pre_dat <- asc_to_pupilpre(path_to_file,
                               label,
                               recorded_eye,
                               trial_start_msg,
                               id_pattern,
                               trial_end_msg)
head(ppl_pre_dat$pplpreData)
#head(ppl_pre_dat$rawMessages)


```
```{r}
# Extract StartTrial timestamps from rawMessages, join to pplpreData, compute Time

library(dplyr)

# rawMessages in your data uses columns: time, text (we saw these earlier)

msg_df <- ppl_pre_dat$rawMessages

# defensive check

if(!all(c("time","text") %in% names(msg_df))) {
stop("rawMessages does not contain expected columns 'time' and 'text'.")
}

# Extract StartTrial lines and parse TRIAL_INDEX

start_pattern <- "var StartTrial [0-9]+"
start_msgs <- msg_df[grep(start_pattern, msg_df$text), , drop = FALSE]

if(nrow(start_msgs) == 0) stop("No StartTrial messages found in rawMessages!")

start_msgs$TRIAL_INDEX <- as.numeric(sub(".*StartTrial ([0-9]+).*", "\1", start_msgs$text))

# Build start_times (TRIAL_INDEX, start_ts)

start_times <- start_msgs %>%
select(TRIAL_INDEX, start_ts = time) %>%
distinct(TRIAL_INDEX, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Attach start times to the full pplpreData

ppd <- ppl_pre_dat$pplpreData

# Ensure TRIAL_INDEX numeric types match

ppd$TRIAL_INDEX <- as.numeric(ppd$TRIAL_INDEX)
start_times$TRIAL_INDEX <- as.numeric(start_times$TRIAL_INDEX)

# Left join so each sample gets its trial's start timestamp (NA for non-trial rows)

ppd <- left_join(ppd, start_times, by = "TRIAL_INDEX")

# If asc_to_pupilpre produced an in_trial_shifted column (recommended), ensure it exists

if(!("in_trial_shifted" %in% names(ppd))) {
warning("in_trial_shifted not present in pplpreData. If you want pre-trial samples, ensure asc_to_pupilpre yields in_trial_shifted.")

# as a fallback, create it identical to in_trial (not ideal)

ppd$in_trial_shifted <- ppd$in_trial
}

# Compute Time relative to StartTrial: Time = TIMESTAMP - start_ts

# Note: TIMESTAMP is the sample timestamp column created in asc_to_pupilpre

if(!("TIMESTAMP" %in% names(ppd))) stop("TIMESTAMP column not found in pplpreData.")

ppd <- ppd %>% mutate(Time = TIMESTAMP - start_ts)

# Quick diagnostics

cat("Global Time range (min to max):", min(ppd$Time, na.rm = TRUE), "to", max(ppd$Time, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Number of rows with Time < 0:", sum(ppd$Time < 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Example start_times (first 10):\n")
print(head(start_times, 10))

# assign dat_time as the full dataset with Time for downstream steps

dat_time <- ppd

```
```{r}
# check_msg_time equivalent diagnostic if you want to verify alignments:

# for each trial, show how many samples exist in [-400,0)

dat_time %>%
group_by(TRIAL_INDEX) %>%
summarise(n_pre400 = sum(Time >= -400 & Time < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
min_time = min(Time, na.rm = TRUE),
.groups = "drop") %>%
summary()

```

```{r}
# Now filter out practice trials and popup trials (do this AFTER Time exists and after cleaning)

# This will remove whole trials (including their pretrial samples) for those trial indices.

dat4 <- subset(dat4, !(TRIAL_INDEX %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4, 14, 15, 16, 17)))

bad_events <- c("sub1.1", "sub1.2", "sub1.3", "sub1.4",
"sub1.14", "sub1.15", "sub1.16", "sub1.17")

dat4 <- dat4[! as.character(dat4$Event) %in% bad_events, ]
dat4$Event <- droplevels(dat4$Event)


```

```{r}

```
```{r}
ppl_plot_avg(data = dat6, xlim = c(-400, 5000), Column = "Pupil",
             Condition1 = NULL, Condition2 = NULL, Cond1Labels = NA, 
             Cond2Labels = NA, ErrorBar = FALSE, ErrorBand=TRUE, PupilPreTheme = TRUE) 
```
```{r}
dat6$condition <- 0 #ini at 0
cond <- 'none'
for(i in 1:length(dat6$Subject)){ #for each sample in our dataset
    tmp <- dat6$SAMPLE_MESSAGE[i] #check whether there's a message
    if(!is.na(tmp)){ #if there is
        tmp <- regexpr( 'difficulty [0-9]+', dat6$SAMPLE_MESSAGE[i]) #check whether 'difficulty ##' is in the message
        if(!is.na(tmp) && tmp != -1){ #if so
            cond <- regmatches(dat6$SAMPLE_MESSAGE[i],tmp)        
            cond <- as.numeric(regmatches(cond,regexpr("[0-9]+",cond))) #set 'cond' to the type 
        }
    }
    dat6$condition[i] <- cond #and add this to the new condition variable that we added above
}
dat6$difficulty <- as.factor(dat6$condition)

#now we can plot:
ppl_plot_avg(data = dat6, xlim = c(-400, 5000), Column = "Pupil", 
             Condition1 = "difficulty", Condition2 = NULL, 
             ErrorBar = FALSE, ErrorBand=TRUE, PupilPreTheme = FALSE)
```
